dedupe_keys.name: cosima co simulation of communication networks with multi agent systems in energy systems

description: cosima is an open-source co-simulation framework that couples the OMNeT++ network simulator with the mosaik smart-grid co-simulation framework, so that messages exchanged by agents controlling an energy system are delayed, lost or reordered as they would be over a real communication network. It was developed at OFFIS and the University of Oldenburg and described by Oest, Frost, Radtke and Lehnhoff in a 2022 paper (arXiv 2209.12550), which reports experiments with up to 50 agents. Agents are written with the mango agent framework; mosaik runs the power system simulators, and cosima synchronises simulated time between mosaik and OMNeT++ so that communication latency feeds back into control decisions. The repository targets OMNeT++ 5.6.2 and mosaik 3.0 or later and includes example scenarios, with documentation on Read the Docs and a project website. Coverage: generic scenarios; network models from OMNeT++ and INET. Format and access: source code on GitHub, free; the repository licence is the GNU LGPL version 2.1. Caveats: a research tool tied to specific OMNeT++ and mosaik versions; scenario setup needs knowledge of all three frameworks. Simulation uses: studying how communication network failures, congestion or cyber attacks affect distributed control of power grids, which makes it a tool for energy and telecom interdependency analysis. Related records: mosaik and OMNeT++ are the frameworks it couples, and ns-3 and GNS3 are other network simulators.
